instructions: Netlify's validated OAuth for tooling is the CLI: `netlify login` opens a browser authorization page and approving it is the whole consent — no token is typed or pasted.
The manual equivalent is installing the Netlify CLI (docs.netlify.com/cli/get-started) and running `netlify login` yourself.
The credential lands in the CLI's own machine-local config, outside this repository.

run.why: Install the official Netlify CLI if missing, then authenticate: the browser opens an authorization page and the command waits for your approval. No token is typed or pasted.

instructions: The whole path is the terminal: `netlify init` creates the site and links this repository, `netlify env:set` configures it, `netlify deploy --prod` ships. No dashboard step stands between a fresh clone and a live URL.

`netlify.toml` is the deployment and is committed: its build command must run `npx convex deploy --cmd 'pnpm build'` so backend and frontend ship together. Netlify treats the file as authoritative, so it overrides the dashboard.

Netlify holds `CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY` and public keys only — set them with `netlify env:set <NAME> --secret`. Every backend secret stays in the prod Convex deployment env, never in Netlify or `netlify.toml`.
Secret values never appear in `netlify.toml`; it is committed, so a value written into it is published.
